name: Congenital stenosis of the inferior vena cava

criteria.description: Radiologic evidence of inferior vena cava stenosis or narrowing on venography, CT, or MRI
Presence of lower extremity venous hypertension symptoms such as edema or venous claudication
Exclusion of acquired causes of IVC stenosis such as thrombosis or external compression
History or evidence of congenital vascular anomaly without prior trauma or surgery

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiologic confirmation of IVC stenosis plus clinical signs of venous hypertension with exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on imaging and clinical correlation; no standardized formal criteria exist.

pathognomonic.notes: Pain and cramping in legs due to impaired venous return
Persistent swelling due to venous congestion
Collateral venous circulation visible on abdominal wall

common.symptomName: Venous stasis dermatitis of lower limbs
common.notes: Skin changes secondary to chronic venous insufficiency
searchTerms: skin inflammation from poor leg circulation
leg skin changes due to vein problems

common.symptomName: Recurrent lower extremity deep vein thrombosis
common.notes: Increased risk due to venous flow obstruction
searchTerms: repeated deep vein blood clots in legs

common.symptomName: Fatigue in lower limbs on exertion
common.notes: Due to impaired venous return and tissue hypoxia
searchTerms: weakness in lower limbs when walking

common.notes: Related to collateral venous circulation or congestion

occasional.notes: Audible turbulent flow over stenotic segment
searchTerms: abdominal vein sound heard with stethoscope
abnormal blood flow noise in abdomen

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary embolism secondary to venous thrombosis
searchTerms: lung blood clot from leg thrombosis
lung clot secondary to vein clots

rare.symptomName: Lower limb ulceration due to chronic venous insufficiency
rare.notes: Chronic skin breakdown from venous hypertension
searchTerms: leg ulcers from poor vein function
lower limb wounds due to vein problems

laboratory: Elevated D-dimer in cases with thrombosis
Normal inflammatory markers unless thrombophlebitis present
imaging: Venography showing focal stenosis or narrowing of the inferior vena cava
CT or MRI demonstrating congenital narrowing without external compression
Doppler ultrasound revealing impaired venous flow
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; presumed sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Venous pressure measurements indicating elevated venous hypertension

distinguishingFeatures: History of trauma, surgery, or thrombosis
Imaging shows post-inflammatory or post-thrombotic changes
Acute onset with thrombus visible on imaging
Mass or tumor compressing the IVC on imaging
Symptoms related to underlying compressive lesion

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe lower limb swelling
Signs of pulmonary embolism such as sudden dyspnea or chest pain
Progressive venous ulceration or skin necrosis
